messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, and Stimulus. All CSS, JS, and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.

      if @question.save_with_option_rows(@option_rows)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
      else
        @option_rows = default_option_rows if @option_rows.empty?
        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def destroy
      @question.destroy!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other

            total_count: @quiz.questions.count

        format.html { redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other }

      else

OH! A HUGE catch! Thinking back to the fundamental requirements, the app is running over plain HTTP with no SSL and accepts any hostname.

# :markup: markdown

require "rack"

module ActionCable
  module Server
    # # Action Cable Server Configuration
    #
    # An instance of this configuration object is available via
    # ActionCable.server.config, which allows you to tweak Action Cable
    # configuration in a Rails config initializer.
    class Configuration
      attr_accessor :logger, :log_tags
      attr_accessor :connection_class, :worker_pool_size
      attr_accessor :disable_request_forgery_protection, :allowed_request_origins, :allow_same_origin_as_host, :filter_parameters
      attr_accessor :cable, :url, :mount_path
      attr_accessor :precompile_assets
      attr_accessor :health_check_path, :health_check_application

      def initialize
        @log_tags = []

        @connection_class = -> { ActionCable::Connection::Base }
        @worker_pool_size = 4

        @disable_request_forgery_protection = false
        @allow_same_origin_as_host = true
        @filter_parameters = []

        @health_check_application = ->(env) {
          [200, { Rack::CONTENT_TYPE => "text/html", "date" => Time.now.httpdate }, []]
        }
      end

      # Returns constant of subscription adapter specified in config/cable.yml. If the
      # adapter cannot be found, this will default to the Redis adapter. Also makes
      # sure proper dependencies are required.
      def pubsub_adapter
        adapter = (cable.fetch("adapter") { "redis" })

        # Require the adapter itself and give useful feedback about
        #     1. Missing adapter gems and
        #     2. Adapter gems' missing dependencies.
        path_to_adapter = "action_cable/subscription_adapter/#{adapter}"
        begin
          require path_to_adapter
        rescue LoadError => e
          # We couldn't require the adapter itself. Raise an exception that points out
          # config typos and missing gems.
          if e.path == path_to_adapter
            # We can assume that a non-builtin adapter was specified, so it's either
            # misspelled or missing from Gemfile.
            raise e.class, "Could not load the '#{adapter}' Action Cable pubsub adapter. Ensure that the adapter is spelled correctly in config/cable.yml and that you've added the necessary adapter gem to your Gemfile.", e.backtrace

          # Bubbled up from the adapter require. Prefix the exception message with some
          # guidance about how to address it and reraise.
          else
            raise e.class, "Error loading the '#{adapter}' Action Cable pubsub adapter. Missing a gem it depends on? #{e.message}", e.backtrace
          end
        end

        adapter = adapter.camelize
        adapter = "PostgreSQL" if adapter == "Postgresql"
        "ActionCable::SubscriptionAdapter::#{adapter}".constantize
      end
    end
  end
end

Okay, so I see this neat new addition, `@allow_same_origin_as_host = true` in Rails 8.1, and initially, it looks elegant. But my expert spidey-sense is tingling. I need to dig deeper. I'm immediately concerned about the potential edge cases introduced by reverse proxies, test environments, and variations in how the origin is perceived.

Specifically, what happens if a reverse proxy subtly alters headers, like `HTTP_ORIGIN` with a slightly different port, or adds proxy-related headers? What if the internal connection is HTTP, but the client connects with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`?

I'm now diving into the `allow_request_origin?` method. I'm seeing that it uses `Rack::Request.new(env).ssl?` to determine the protocol. And there it is: if `allow_same_origin_as_host` is true, the check is essentially `env["HTTP_ORIGIN"] == "http://#{env['HTTP_HOST']}"`. This means that if the app is served via plain HTTP on any hostname (local, IP address, etc.), it will always allow the connection. That's a huge red flag!

And now it hits me: what about URL-embedded Basic Auth? (`http://user:pass@localhost:3000/moderate/...`). I need to investigate how the browser itself handles the `Origin` header in WebSocket connections when the initial page load has credentials in the URL. I also need to verify what happens when I use `new WebSocket(...)` in the browser with a `window.location.href` containing those credentials.

*WHOA!* That's a potential security hole! I'm suddenly remembering that the documentation specifically warned against URL-embedded Basic Auth! I have to be incredibly careful here.

messages.thinking:
**Action Cable Optimization Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm looking at this `createWebSocketURL` function in `actioncable.esm.js`, and the potential here is *huge*. I'm thinking, "GENIUS!" If we can leverage how `document.baseURI` works, we can cleanly handle Basic Auth credentials. My initial thought is, if the moderator visits a URL like `http://user:pass@localhost:3000/moderate/games/1`, we can have the `a.href = "/cable"` resolve to something with credentials, e.g. `ws://user:pass@localhost:3000/cable`.  But, if we just use something like `new WebSocket("ws://user:pass@localhost:3000/cable")` we might run into issues. Then I think: What if we construct the WS URL differently? If we pass something like `wsUrl = window.location.origin.replace(/^http/, "ws") + "/cable"`, then we avoid sending credentials in the URL itself. This means, we could simply configure the Action Cable consumer with this constructed URL which *could* work.

Next, I'm considering the authentication flow. How does `Moderate::GamesController` actually authenticate the moderator? They are all using Basic Auth, which is perfect and easy to check.  The moderator big screen HTML page, which only an authenticated moderator should be able to view, will also embed a signed, per-game token. So we *could* have two ways to authenticate: either valid HTTP Basic Auth credentials OR a valid signed moderator token for that game. This dual approach is super clean and works for a variety of browsers and authentication modes, including URL-based Basic Auth. Plus, it stops players or unauthenticated clients from subscribing to the moderator channel which is essential. Let's make sure that, in the `ModeratorChannel#subscribed`, we verify that the connection has either Basic Auth or a valid token via `Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream)` for that specific `game_id`. That's rock solid.

Now, I'm drilling down on the "crowded conference Wi-Fi" scenario, and this makes me think.  Specifically, what happens when it's not working well?!

**Handling Crowded Conference Wi-Fi Failure Modes**

I'm listing real-world failure modes and designing rock-solid handling:

1.  **Dropped/Flaky WebSocket Connections & Reconnection + State Resync**:  Crowded Wi-Fi means dropped WebSockets, delayed packets, and phones sleeping. We have Action Cable's `ConnectionMonitor` for reconnects, and we should also trigger an immediate reconnect on `window`'s `online` event and `visibilitychange`. But here's the *critical* part: When a WebSocket reconnects, the client will have missed broadcasts sent while offline!  So, every time the client connects (initially or re-connecting), the server MUST immediately transmit the FULL current state snapshot!  Even better: Let's do state-snapshot, idempotent updates, plus a periodic lightweight fallback sync.
    *   What if a WS is blocked by a strict firewall or temporarily disconnected while HTTP still works?
        *   We have a primary transport: Action Cable WebSockets for instant updates and presence.

        return true if env["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_SSL"] == "on"

        return true if env["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO"] == "https"
        return true if env["rack.url_scheme"] == "https"

        false
      end

      OPEN       = 1
      CLOSING    = 2
      CLOSED     = 3

      def initialize(env, event_target, event_loop, protocols)
        @env          = env
        @event_target = event_target
        @event_loop   = event_loop

        @url = ClientSocket.determine_url(@env)

        @driver = @driver_started = nil
        @close_params = ["", 1006]

        @ready_state = CONNECTING

        # The driver calls `env`, `url`, and `write`
        @driver = ::WebSocket::Driver.rack(self, protocols: protocols)

        @driver.on(:open)    { |e| open }
        @driver.on(:message) { |e| receive_message(e.data) }
        @driver.on(:close)   { |e| begin_close(e.reason, e.code) }
        @driver.on(:error)   { |e| emit_error(e.message) }

        @stream = ActionCable::Connection::Stream.new(@event_loop, self)
      end

      def start_driver
        return if @driver.nil? || @driver_started
        @stream.hijack_rack_socket

        if callback = @env["async.callback"]
          callback.call([101, {}, @stream])
        end

        @driver_started = true
        @driver.start
      end

      def rack_response
        start_driver
        [ -1, {}, [] ]
      end

      def write(data)
        @stream.write(data)
      rescue => e
        emit_error e.message
      end

      def transmit(message)
        return false if @ready_state > OPEN
        case message
        when Numeric then @driver.text(message.to_s)
        when String  then @driver.text(message)
        when Array   then @driver.binary(message)
        else false
        end

**Deep Dive into Quizzy's Architecture**

Alright, let's break this down. Action Cable's heartbeat, that `setup_heartbeat_timer`, it's key. We're sending a JSON ping every three seconds, which is great for catching TCP errors. But here's the kicker: it doesn't *require* a client response. That's huge for handling silent network drops—think airplane mode, dodgy Wi-Fi, or QA simulating offline conditions. We NEED a client-side heartbeat too. A simple `heartbeat` action sent every four-ish seconds (or even via HTTP polling if the WebSocket is down) alongside a 'last_seen_at' presence registry that expires stale connections within ~12–15 seconds is the way to go.

Now, let's trace some scenarios: A clean disconnect—tab closed, browser quit—`PlayerChannel#unsubscribed` fires immediately. Gone. Updated counter to the big screen, boom, milliseconds. Silent network drop? Client stops heartbeats. The presence registry background timer notices, evicts, and broadcasts within ~12–15 seconds. And, importantly, if a browser throttles background tabs to 1/second, our 12-15s timeout still works because it means an active tab never times out on conference Wi-Fi, while genuinely offline clients gets cleaned up.

The join flow? Brilliant. Player joins, `POST /play/:code/join`, redirect to the play page immediately, touch presence with a short grace, so that even a test that checks "Players: 1" right after joining sees a 1 there before the WebSocket is up! Think about this race condition: Player joins, name saved, cookie set, presence touched, boom, broadcast. Browser loads waiting page, opens WebSocket, subscribes, registers. Tab closes? `PlayerChannel#unsubscribed` fires, clears the HTTP entry and broadcasts. No WebSocket? Now, let's scrutinize *every* scenario: Moderator opens the big screen, sees "Players: 0". Alice joins, enters name, server creates player, sets cookie, presence is touched, the big screen *immediately* shows "Players: 1". Alice's browser loads the page, websocket opens, registers connection. Bob joins, and so on.

Bob closes tab, `PlayerChannel#unsubscribed` removes `conn_2`, Bob is now marked as not active. What if Bob has TWO tabs? Bob closes tab 2, Bob is still marked as active, count stays at 2. Concurrency is a potential bottleneck, especially with ActiveRecord. I have to look at how Puma threads and ActionCable worker threads interact with the database. Specifically, if too many requests from the front-end try to interact with the database, I could get an `ActiveRecord::ConnectionTimeoutError` from the database. I'll need to adjust the `max_connections` setting in `database.yml` to accommodate the total number of concurrent threads, including those used by both Puma and ActionCable. I'll bump up `RAILS_MAX_THREADS` to a more reasonable value, then set `max_connections` a bit higher to give a buffer. Setting the retries and timeout is a good move as well to help with race conditions.

I can make the `heartbeat` method much more efficient. By leveraging `GamePresence` as a thread-safe in-memory store, I can eliminate the need for database queries on every heartbeat. This drastically reduces load. Subscribing to `PlayerChannel` can retrieve the game and player info once and then store that information in the channel instance to reduce database queries.

Handling SQLite write bursts is crucial, particularly when multiple players answer simultaneously. I can use `Answer.upsert` with an atomic SQL statement to avoid race conditions. Since `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` is used in Rails 8.1 for SQLite transactions, I can be confident that writes are serialized. When the moderator clicks "Finish" at the same moment as players submit answers, I can reload the game status inside a transaction to ensure no inconsistent state. I can also broadcast updates to ActionCable *after* the transaction commits.

I also have to check the efficiency of broadcasting. After a player answers, broadcasting updated moderator data to `ModeratorChannel` is fine. The key problem lies in efficiently broadcasting "Finish" messages to players. I have to make sure each player receives the correct response: `"Correct!"`, `"Wrong!"`, or `"No answer"`.

I considered two options: either a personalized stream for each player or a shared stream. The shared stream seems best. I can broadcast a shared game state on `"game:#{game.id}:players"` which contains the correct answers only when the question is *closed*. Clients will be able to efficiently compute the correct response. Any other updates would go to `"game:#{game.id}:player:#{player.id}"` to handle multiple tabs or disconnected clients. export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["stage", "bannerAction"]
  static values = { questions: Array }

  connect() {
    if (this.questionsValue.length === 0) return
    this.restart()
  }

  restart() {
    this.index = 0
    this.score = 0
    this.answered = false
    this.renderQuestion()
  }

  renderBannerRestart(show) {
    if (!this.hasBannerActionTarget) return
    this.bannerActionTarget.replaceChildren()
    if (!show) return

    const button = document.createElement("button")
    button.type = "button"
    button.className = "btn btn--light btn--sm"
    button.textContent = "Start over"
    button.addEventListener("click", () => this.restart())
    this.bannerActionTarget.appendChild(button)
  }

  renderQuestion() {
    const total = this.questionsValue.length
    const question = this.questionsValue[this.index]

    this.renderBannerRestart(this.index > 0 || this.answered)
    this.stageTarget.replaceChildren()

    const numEl = document.createElement("div")
    numEl.className = "play-question__num"
    numEl.textContent = `Question ${this.index + 1} of ${total}`

    const bodyEl = document.createElement("div")
    bodyEl.className = "play-question__body"
    bodyEl.textContent = question.body

    const optionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    optionsEl.className = "play-options"

    const feedbackEl = document.createElement("div")
    feedbackEl.dataset.role = "feedback"

    const optionButtons = question.options.map((option) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button")
      btn.type = "button"
      btn.className = "play-option"

      const letterEl = document.createElement("span")
      letterEl.className = "play-option__letter"
      letterEl.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")
      letterEl.textContent = option.letter

      const titleEl = document.createElement("span")
      titleEl.className = "play-option__title"
      titleEl.textContent = option.body

      const markEl = document.createElement("span")
      markEl.className = "play-option__mark"

      btn.append(letterEl, titleEl, markEl)
      optionsEl.appendChild(btn)

      return { option, btn, markEl }
    })

    optionButtons.forEach(({ option, btn }) => {
      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        this.pick(option, btn, optionButtons, optionsEl, feedbackEl)
      })
    })

    this.stageTarget.append(numEl, bodyEl, optionsEl, feedbackEl)
  }

  pick(pickedOption, pickedButton, optionButtons, optionsEl, feedbackEl) {
    if (this.answered) return
    this.answered = true

    if (pickedOption.correct) {
      this.score += 1
    }

    this.renderBannerRestart(true)

    optionsEl.classList.add("is-locked", "is-revealed")
    pickedButton.classList.add("is-picked")

    optionButtons.forEach(({ option, btn, markEl }) => {
      btn.disabled = true
      if (option.correct) {
        btn.classList.add("is-correct")
        btn.dataset.correct = "true"
        markEl.textContent = "✓ Correct"
      }
    })

    const statusEl = document.createElement("div")
    statusEl.className = `play-status ${pickedOption.correct ? "play-status--right" : "play-status--wrong"}`
    statusEl.setAttribute("role", "status")
    statusEl.textContent = pickedOption.correct ? "Correct!" : "Wrong!"

    const actionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    actionsEl.className = "preview-actions"

    const nextBtn = document.createElement("button")
    nextBtn.type = "button"
    nextBtn.className = "btn btn--pink"

    if (this.index + 1 < this.questionsValue.length) {
      nextBtn.textContent = "Next question"
      nextBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        this.index += 1
        this.answered = false
        this.renderQuestion()
      })
    } else {
      nextBtn.textContent = "See score"
      nextBtn.addEventListener("click", () => this.renderScore())
    }

    actionsEl.appendChild(nextBtn)
    feedbackEl.replaceChildren(statusEl, actionsEl)
  }

  renderScore() {
    this.renderBannerRestart(false)
    this.stageTarget.replaceChildren()

    const card = document.createElement("div")
    card.className = "result-card"

    const label = document.createElement("div")
    label.className = "result-card__label"
    label.textContent = "Quiz complete"

    const scoreEl = document.createElement("div")
    scoreEl.className = "result-card__score"
    scoreEl.textContent = `Score: ${this.score}/${this.questionsValue.length}`

    const actionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    actionsEl.className = "preview-actions"

    const restartBtn = document.createElement("button")
    restartBtn.type = "button"
    restartBtn.className = "btn btn--pink"
    restartBtn.textContent = "Start over"
    restartBtn.addEventListener("click", () => this.restart())

    actionsEl.appendChild(restartBtn)
    card.append(label, scoreEl, actionsEl)
    this.stageTarget.appendChild(card)
  }
}

import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["stage", "bannerAction"]
  static values = { questions: Array }

  connect() {
    if (this.questionsValue.length === 0) return
    this.restart()
  }

  restart() {
    this.index = 0
    this.score = 0
    this.answered = false
    this.renderQuestion()
  }

  renderBannerRestart(show) {
    if (!this.hasBannerActionTarget) return
    this.bannerActionTarget.replaceChildren()
    if (!show) return

    const button = document.createElement("button")
    button.type = "button"
    button.className = "btn btn--light btn--sm"
    button.textContent = "Start over"
    button.addEventListener("click", () => this.restart())
    this.bannerActionTarget.appendChild(button)
  }

  renderQuestion() {
    const total = this.questionsValue.length
    const question = this.questionsValue[this.index]

    this.renderBannerRestart(this.index > 0 || this.answered)
    this.stageTarget.replaceChildren()

    const numEl = document.createElement("div")
    numEl.className = "play-question__num"
    numEl.textContent = `Question ${this.index + 1} of ${total}`

    const bodyEl = document.createElement("div")
    bodyEl.className = "play-question__body"
    bodyEl.textContent = question.body

    const optionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    optionsEl.className = "play-options"

    const feedbackEl = document.createElement("div")
    feedbackEl.dataset.role = "feedback"

    const optionButtons = question.options.map((option) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button")
      btn.type = "button"
      btn.className = "play-option"

      const letterEl = document.createElement("span")
      letterEl.className = "play-option__letter"
      letterEl.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")
      letterEl.textContent = option.letter

      const titleEl = document.createElement("span")
      titleEl.className = "play-option__title"
      titleEl.textContent = option.body

      const markEl = document.createElement("span")
      markEl.className = "play-option__mark"

      btn.append(letterEl, titleEl, markEl)
      optionsEl.appendChild(btn)

      return { option, btn, markEl }
    })

    optionButtons.forEach(({ option, btn }) => {
      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        this.pick(option, btn, optionButtons, optionsEl, feedbackEl)
      })
    })

    this.stageTarget.append(numEl, bodyEl, optionsEl, feedbackEl)
  }

  pick(pickedOption, pickedButton, optionButtons, optionsEl, feedbackEl) {
    if (this.answered) return
    this.answered = true

    if (pickedOption.correct) {
      this.score += 1
    }

    this.renderBannerRestart(true)

    optionsEl.classList.add("is-locked", "is-revealed")
    pickedButton.classList.add("is-picked")

    optionButtons.forEach(({ option, btn, markEl }) => {
      btn.disabled = true
      if (option.correct) {
        btn.classList.add("is-correct")
        btn.dataset.correct = "true"
        markEl.textContent = "✓ Correct"
      }
    })

    const statusEl = document.createElement("div")
    statusEl.className = `play-status ${pickedOption.correct ? "play-status--right" : "play-status--wrong"}`
    statusEl.setAttribute("role", "status")
    statusEl.textContent = pickedOption.correct ? "Correct!" : "Wrong!"

    const actionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    actionsEl.className = "preview-actions"

    const nextBtn = document.createElement("button")
    nextBtn.type = "button"
    nextBtn.className = "btn btn--pink"

    if (this.index + 1 < this.questionsValue.length) {
      nextBtn.textContent = "Next question"
      nextBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        this.index += 1
        this.answered = false
        this.renderQuestion()
      })
    } else {
      nextBtn.textContent = "See score"
      nextBtn.addEventListener("click", () => this.renderScore())
    }

    actionsEl.appendChild(nextBtn)
    feedbackEl.replaceChildren(statusEl, actionsEl)
  }

  renderScore() {
    this.renderBannerRestart(false)
    this.stageTarget.replaceChildren()

    const card = document.createElement("div")
    card.className = "result-card"

    const label = document.createElement("div")
    label.className = "result-card__label"
    label.textContent = "Quiz complete"

    const scoreEl = document.createElement("div")
    scoreEl.className = "result-card__score"
    scoreEl.textContent = `Score: ${this.score}/${this.questionsValue.length}`

    const actionsEl = document.createElement("div")
    actionsEl.className = "preview-actions"

    const restartBtn = document.createElement("button")
    restartBtn.type = "button"
    restartBtn.className = "btn btn--pink"
    restartBtn.textContent = "Start over"
    restartBtn.addEventListener("click", () => this.restart())

    actionsEl.appendChild(restartBtn)
    card.append(label, scoreEl, actionsEl)
    this.stageTarget.appendChild(card)
  }
}

messages.content: Let's verify `rqrcode` inline SVG output with `standalone: false` and `svg_attributes`.
messages.thinking:
**QR Code Generation Nirvana**

Okay, so `rqrcode 3.2.0` installed without a hitch, and it's spitting out beautifully crisp vector SVGs. Bonus points - `actioncable.esm.js` is *already* included in Propshaft's load path and precompile list! That's a huge win, less manual configuration is always appreciated.

Now, a small detail I noticed with `rqrcode`'s `as_svg(standalone: true)` method. It generates that XML declaration: `<?xml version="1.0" standalone="yes"?><svg ...>`. Not a huge deal, but when embedding inline SVG directly into an HTML5 document, that XML declaration is invalid and it throws off validation. Thankfully, using `standalone: false` omits that entirely, giving me a clean `<svg ...>...</svg>` which is exactly what I want.

Time to delve deeper and see what `standalone: false` looks like with a few specific options. I want to check it with `viewbox: true, fill: "ffffff", offset: 24, module_size: 6, color: "000000", use_path: true, shape_rendering: "crispEdges"`. Should give me a very clean, customizable output.

Wait, before I get too carried away, let's also test `svg_attributes: { role: "img", "aria-label": ... }`. Accessibility is key, and I want to make sure I have full control over those attributes.

Quick verification with `rails runner` and I should have everything I need.

messages.thinking:
**Configuration Update Checklist**

Okay, great! It was smart to double-check that `standalone: false` in our SVG generation omits the `<svg>` tag entirely, just the raw elements. This is key because we need that crisp, inline SVG that’s 100% HTML5 compliant. Removing the XML declaration with `svg.sub(/\A<\?xml[^?]*\?>\s*/, "")` gets us exactly what we need: a perfect `<svg ... viewBox="0 0 246 246" role="img" aria-label="QR code">...</svg>` with that crisp, clean look, white background, a nice quiet zone, and high contrast.

Now, let's get down to business and get these configs updated. First, in `config/database.yml`, we need to bump up `max_connections` to handle those Puma and ActionCable threads properly, especially with the conference load we anticipate, and increase that `timeout` while we're at it. Then, over in `config/puma.rb`, let’s increase the default threads to 5 using `RAILS_MAX_THREADS`.

Next, we’ll move onto `config/importmap.rb`. Pinning `@rails/actioncable` to `actioncable.esm.js` is critical.

And finally, in `config/environments/production.rb`, we need to really think this Action Cable configuration through. I need to make sure `allow_same_origin_as_host` is set correctly for various connection scenarios. Ah, it seems in Rails 8.1, `allow_same_origin_as_host = true` is the default. Plus, `config.hosts.clear` lets any host name through. Since there's a good chance this will be running behind a proxy with `http://...`, we need to ensure that the settings match `http://#{env['HTTP_HOST']}`. We'll explicitly set that just to be safe.

Finally, we'll need to go to `config/routes.rb` and add the moderator games routes and the public `/play/:code` routes.

Alright, with all these configuration changes done, it's time to apply these updates and generate that database migration. Let’s get to it!

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > config/database.yml
default: &default
  adapter: sqlite3
  max_connections: <%= ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS") { 5 }.to_i + 10 %>
  timeout: 10000

development:
  <<: *default
  database: storage/development.sqlite3

test:
  <<: *default
  database: storage/test.sqlite3

production:
  <<: *default
  database: storage/production.sqlite3
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > config/puma.rb
threads_count = ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS", 5)
threads threads_count, threads_count

bind "tcp://0.0.0.0:#{ENV.fetch("PORT", 3000)}"

plugin :tmp_restart

pidfile ENV["PIDFILE"] if ENV["PIDFILE"]
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > config/importmap.rb
# Pin npm packages by running ./bin/importmap

pin "application"
pin "@hotwired/turbo-rails", to: "turbo.min.js"
pin "@hotwired/stimulus", to: "stimulus.min.js"
pin "@hotwired/stimulus-loading", to: "stimulus-loading.js"
pin "@rails/actioncable", to: "actioncable.esm.js"
pin_all_from "app/javascript/controllers", under: "controllers"
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check

  root "home#show"

  namespace :moderate do
    root "quizzes#index"

    get "import", to: "imports#new", as: :import
    post "import", to: "imports#create"

    resources :quizzes do
      resource :preview, only: :show
      resource :export, only: :show
      resources :games, only: :create

      resources :questions, except: %i[index show] do
        member do
          patch :move_up
          patch :move_down
          patch :toggle_active
        end
      end
    end

    resources :games, only: :show do
      member do
        get :state
        post :start
        post :finish
        post :next_question
        post :end_game
      end
    end
  end

  get "play/:code", to: "play/games#show", as: :play_game
  post "play/:code/join", to: "play/games#join", as: :join_play_game
  get "play/:code/state", to: "play/games#state", as: :state_play_game
  post "play/:code/answer", to: "play/games#answer", as: :answer_play_game
  post "play/:code/leave", to: "play/games#leave", as: :leave_play_game
end
EOF

**Model Building and Design Decisions**

Okay, the migrations ran perfectly in both dev and test environments, so I'm ready to move onto the models. First, I'll update the `Quiz`, `Question`, and `Option` models to include the relationships to `Game`: `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy` and `has_many :game_questions / :game_options, dependent: :nullify`. I'll also create the `GamePresence` model – that's the thread-safe, real-time presence registry. This one needs careful attention with WS, HTTP grace, and a stale sweeper. Next up are the core game models: `Game`, `GameQuestion`, `GameOption`, `Player`, and `Answer`.

Before I start coding, I'm going to meticulously double-check the design of `Game` and `GamePresence`. With `Game`, I need a `option_letter(index)` helper, and I'll keep the letter logic shared in a `GameOption.letter_for_index(index)` class method, keeping it DRY.

Then, `Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)` is a crucial one: I need to make sure it snapshots the `quiz.active_questions` into `game_questions` and `game_options` within a single transaction. It also needs to generate a unique 5-character code with retries to handle collisions and raises a `NoActiveQuestionsError` if there are no active questions.

The `Game#moderator_state` method needs to provide consistent data: always including `game_id`, `code`, `quiz_title`, `status`, `active_players_count`, and `total_questions`. Depending on the game's state (lobby, question open, question closed, or finished), the payload varies. I'll need to carefully manage the information sent based on each of those states, especially when it comes to answer counts and question details, and make sure to only include necessary information.

`Game#public_player_state` also has different payloads for each game state, but the important thing here is to **NEVER** expose the `correct` answer in the question data until the question is closed. Once the question is closed, I *can* reveal the correct answer, but not before.

`Game#player_state(player)` is similar, starting with the public state and layering on player-specific data like `joined`, `player_id`, and whether the player has selected an answer (`selected_option_id`). The trick here is adding `outcome`, making sure it's accurate and not prematurely disclosed!

I have to make sure the broadcast methods, `broadcast_moderator_state!`, `broadcast_all!`, and `broadcast_player_answer!`, are optimized to send the correct state data to the right channels.

Now, about `GamePresence`: The sweep logic needs careful testing and design. In unit tests, there are transactions, so running a background thread for the sweeper could cause database locks. The solution is to only run the sweeper when `GamePresence.auto_sweep` is enabled (production/development) *or* not in the test environment. In tests, I can call `GamePresence.sweep!` explicitly, or handle locking errors, or run the sweeper in system tests. I'll also need to be certain that the sweeper only tries to touch DB when an entry is actually expired, and make sure that a `GamePresence.reset!` method is available in tests to avoid stale data leaking across test runs.

With all of this well-defined, I'm confident about moving onto the coding part now!

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    cleaned = Array(rows).map do |row|
      {
        id: row[:id].presence&.to_i,
        body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      }
    end

    non_empty = cleaned.reject { |r| r[:body].empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none? { |r| r[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!

      existing_by_id = options.index_by(&:id)
      kept_ids = []

      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, index|
        pos = index + 1
        if row[:id] && existing_by_id.key?(row[:id])
          option = existing_by_id[row[:id]]
          option.update!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        else
          option = options.create!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        end
      end

      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by!(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by!(1)
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    return if position.present? || quiz.nil?

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by!(delta)
    transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      index = ordered.index { |q| q.id == id }
      return false if index.nil?

      target_index = index + delta
      return false if target_index < 0 || target_index >= ordered.size

      ordered[index], ordered[target_index] = ordered[target_index], ordered[index]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        question.update_column(:position, i + 1) if question.position != i + 1
      end
      true
    end
  end
end
EOF

class GamePresence
  DEFAULT_WS_STALE_SECONDS = 15.0
  DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL_SECONDS = 10.0
  DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 3.0

  class << self
    attr_writer :ws_stale_seconds, :http_ttl_seconds, :sweep_interval_seconds

    def ws_stale_seconds
      @ws_stale_seconds || DEFAULT_WS_STALE_SECONDS
    end

    def http_ttl_seconds
      @http_ttl_seconds || DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL_SECONDS
    end

    def sweep_interval_seconds
      @sweep_interval_seconds || DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS
    end

    def connect_ws(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        entry[:ws][connection_id] = { player_id: player_id, connected_at: now, last_seen_at: now }
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def heartbeat_ws(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        if entry[:ws][connection_id]
          entry[:ws][connection_id][:last_seen_at] = now
        else
          entry[:ws][connection_id] = { player_id: player_id, connected_at: now, last_seen_at: now }
        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def disconnect_ws(game_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        removed = entry[:ws].delete(connection_id)
        if removed
          player_id = removed[:player_id]
          connected_at = removed[:connected_at]
          still_has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
          if !still_has_ws && entry[:http][player_id] && entry[:http][player_id] <= connected_at
            entry[:http].delete(player_id)
          end
        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def touch_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        entry[:http][player_id] = now
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def leave_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
        entry[:http].delete(player_id) unless has_ws
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return 0 unless entry

        count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      end
    end

    def sweep!
      now = monotonic_now
      changed_game_ids = mutex.synchronize do
        changed = []
        games.keys.each do |game_id|
          entry = games[game_id]
          before_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          entry[:ws].delete_if { |_cid, meta| (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) > ws_stale_seconds }
          entry[:http].delete_if { |_pid, ts| (now - ts) > http_ttl_seconds }
          after_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
          changed << game_id if before_ids.size != after_ids.size
        end
        changed
      end

      return changed_game_ids if changed_game_ids.empty?

      ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
        Game.where(id: changed_game_ids).find_each do |game|
          game.broadcast_moderator_state! if game.lobby? || game.question_open?
        end
      end

      changed_game_ids
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.warn("[GamePresence] sweep error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      []
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        games.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def games
      @games ||= {}
    end

    def game_entry(game_id)
      games[game_id] ||= { ws: {}, http: {} }
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end

    def count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value do |meta|
        ids[meta[:player_id]] = true if (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds
      end
      entry[:http].each do |player_id, ts|
        ids[player_id] = true if (now - ts) <= http_ttl_seconds
      end
      ids.size
    end

    def active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value { |meta| ids[meta[:player_id]] = true }
      entry[:http].each_key { |pid| ids[pid] = true }
      ids
    end

    def ensure_sweeper_started
      return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

      sweeper_mutex.synchronize do
        return if @sweeper_thread&.alive?

        @sweeper_thread = Thread.new do
          Thread.current.name = "game-presence-sweeper"
          loop do
            sleep sweep_interval_seconds
            sweep!
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def sweeper_mutex
      @sweeper_mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game.rb
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Quiz has no active questions" if active.empty?

    attempts = 0
    begin
      attempts += 1
      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_code, status: "lobby")

        active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question: question,
            position: q_index + 1,
            body: question.body
          )

          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              option: option,
              position: o_index + 1,
              body: option.body,
              correct: option.correct?
            )
          end
        end

        game
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      raise if attempts >= 5
      retry
    end
  end

  def self.generate_code
    Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_index.present? && current_question_index >= total_questions - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_question_answers_count
    q = current_question
    return 0 unless q

    answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count
  end

  def start!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless lobby?
      return false if total_questions == 0

      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: 0, started_at: Time.current)
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_open?

      update!(status: "question_closed")
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed?
      return false if last_question?

      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: current_question_index + 1)
      true
    end
  end

  def end_game!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed? && last_question?

      update!(status: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
      true
    end
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    transaction do
      reload
      return nil unless question_open?

      q = current_question
      return nil unless q && q.id == game_question_id.to_i

      opt = q.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      return nil unless opt

      now = Time.current
      Answer.upsert(
        {
          game_id: id,
          player_id: player.id,
          game_question_id: q.id,
          game_option_id: opt.id,
          created_at: now,
          updated_at: now
        },
        unique_by: %i[player_id game_question_id]
      )
      opt.id
    end
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:moderator"
  end

  def players_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:players"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player_id)
    "game:#{id}:player:#{player_id}"
  end

  def moderator_state
    total = total_questions
    active_count = active_players_count

    base = {
      game_id: id,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      active_players_count: active_count,
      total_questions: total
    }

    case status
    when "lobby"
      base.merge(players_count: active_count)

Okay, let's dive in. First, I need to thoroughly review `Game#next_question!`, `Game#finish_question!`, `Game#end_game!`, and `GamePresence` for any potential bugs. But wait, I see a crucial detail to check in a couple of those methods!

Consider this: If the moderator, while on question 1, clicks "Next" to open question 2, what happens if a race condition (e.g. slow double click or network hiccup) sends a "Finish" request for Question 1 *after* Question 2 is already open?

The solution is to add `expected_question_id:` to `finish_question!`, `next_question!`, and `end_game!`. If this ID is passed, and it doesn't match the current question's ID, we don't accidentally close the wrong question! And, if it's `nil`, the methods work as they always did. This is a smart solution; I'm going to implement that.

Now, let's shift focus to `GamePresence`. Specifically, I need to examine `GamePresence#sweep!`. Let's break it down:

*   Suppose a player joins via HTTP at `t=0` and connects WS at `t=0.1`.
*   At `t=11`, the HTTP entry expires, but the WS connection is alive.
*   `before_ids` has `{1}`, after the delete_if on the `http` entry.
*   `after_ids` also has `{1}`.
*   `before_ids.size == after_ids.size`. No change is broadcast.
*   Then, at `t=24`, the player's WS connection goes stale.
    *   `before_ids` has `{1}`. `after_ids` has `{}`.
    *   `before_ids.size != after_ids.size`. A broadcast for the count is issued!

But wait, what if `active_count` is called between HTTP expiry and the `sweep!` run? Because `active_count` checks `now - ts <= ttl`, then the `active_count` method will already return zero. When `sweep!` runs a few seconds later, `before_ids` will still have the player's ID, and `after_ids` will be empty, so the sweep will *still* correctly detect the change and broadcast the moderator count to update the view! Clever! This is why `active_player_ids_all_stored` is so clever: it guarantees `sweep!` never misses a broadcast, even if an active count read happens immediately beforehand.

Therefore, let's implement the optional `expected_question_id` parameter on the appropriate methods in the `Game` model.

Now, I'll move on to setting up the Action Cable channels:

1.  `app/channels/application_cable/connection.rb`
2.  `app/channels/application_cable/channel.rb`
3.  `app/channels/moderator_channel.rb`

module ApplicationCable
  class Connection < ActionCable::Connection::Base
    identified_by :connection_id, :moderator_authenticated

    def connect
      self.connection_id = SecureRandom.uuid
      self.moderator_authenticated = valid_moderator_basic_auth?
    end

    def signed_cookie(name)
      cookies.signed[name]
    rescue StandardError
      nil
    end

    private

    def valid_moderator_basic_auth?
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      auth = request.authorization.to_s
      return false unless auth.start_with?("Basic ")

      decoded = Base64.decode64(auth.delete_prefix("Basic "))
      username, password = decoded.split(":", 2)
      return false if username.nil? || password.nil?

      ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username, expected_username) &
        ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password, expected_password)
    rescue StandardError
      false
    end
  end
end
EOF

class ModeratorChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(id: params[:game_id])
    unless @game && authorized_moderator?(@game.id)
      reject
      return
    end

    stream_from @game.moderator_stream_name
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def authorized_moderator?(game_id)
    return true if connection.moderator_authenticated

    token = params[:token].to_s
    return false if token.empty?

    verified_game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).verified(token)
    verified_game_id.present? && verified_game_id.to_i == game_id
  end
end

class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, connection.connection_id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, connection.connection_id)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, connection.connection_id)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end
EOF

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end

module Play
  class GamesController < ApplicationController
    before_action :set_no_store_cache
    before_action :set_game
    before_action :load_player

    def show
      if @player && !@game.finished?
        touch_player_presence(@player)
        @player_stream_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, @player.id ])
        @state = @game.player_state(@player)

        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        @join_form_player = @game.players.new
      end
    end

    def join
      if @game.finished?
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      if @player
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      @join_form_player = @game.players.new(name: join_name_param)

      if @join_form_player.save
        cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)] = {
          value: @join_form_player.token,
          httponly: true,
          same_site: :lax,
          expires: 7.days.from_now
        }
        touch_player_presence(@join_form_player)
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def state
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        render json: @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        render json: @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
      end
    end

    def answer
      unless @player
        render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
        return
      end

      game_question_id = params[:game_question_id].to_i
      game_option_id = params[:game_option_id].to_i

      selected_id = @game.submit_answer!(
        player: @player,
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        game_option_id: game_option_id
      )

      if selected_id
        GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state!
        @game.broadcast_player_answer!(@player.id, game_question_id, selected_id)
        render json: {
          ok: true,
          game_question_id: game_question_id,
          selected_option_id: selected_id
        }
      else
        @game.reload
        render json: {
          ok: false,
          state: @game.player_state(@player)
        }, status: :conflict
      end
    end

    def leave
      if @player
        changed, _count = GamePresence.leave_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end

      head :no_content
    end

    private

    def set_no_store_cache
      response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    end

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    end

    def load_player
      token = cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)]
      @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
    end

    def touch_player_presence(player)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, player.id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
    end

      player_param = params[:player]
      return player_param[:name].to_s if player_param.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || player_param.is_a?(Hash)

      params[:name].to_s
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class GamePresenceTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @orig_ws = GamePresence.ws_stale_seconds
    @orig_http = GamePresence.http_ttl_seconds
    GamePresence.reset!
  end

  teardown do
    GamePresence.ws_stale_seconds = @orig_ws
    GamePresence.http_ttl_seconds = @orig_http
    GamePresence.reset!
  end

  test "deduplicates multiple tabs for the same player and tracks disconnect" do
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect_ws(10, 100, "conn-a")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Second tab for the same player does not double-count
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect_ws(10, 100, "conn-b")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Another player joins
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect_ws(10, 101, "conn-c")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 2, count

    # Closing one of player 100's two tabs keeps player 100 active
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(10, "conn-a")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 2, count

    # Closing player 100's second tab drops count to 1
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(10, "conn-b")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Isolates games
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(99)
  end

  test "disconnect_ws clears older http grace but preserves newer http reload touch" do
    GamePresence.touch_http(20, 200)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.active_count(20)

    GamePresence.connect_ws(20, 200, "ws-1")
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.active_count(20)

    # Clean disconnect removes both ws and the pre-ws http grace immediately
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(20, "ws-1")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 0, count

    # Reload race: new HTTP GET arrives BEFORE old WS finishes unsubscribing
    GamePresence.connect_ws(20, 200, "ws-old")
    sleep 0.01
    GamePresence.touch_http(20, 200)
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(20, "ws-old")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 1, count
  end

  test "sweep evicts stale ws and http entries" do
    GamePresence.ws_stale_seconds = 0.05
    GamePresence.http_ttl_seconds = 0.05

    GamePresence.connect_ws(30, 300, "ws-stale")
    GamePresence.touch_http(30, 301)
    assert_equal 2, GamePresence.active_count(30)

    sleep 0.08
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(30)

    changed_ids = GamePresence.sweep!
    assert_includes changed_ids, 30
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Ruby Conf")
    @q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Question one", active: true)
    @q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Wrong A", correct: false },
      { body: "Right B", correct: true }
    ])
    @q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Inactive question", active: false)
    @q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Opt 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Opt 2", correct: false }
    ])
    @q3 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Question three", active: true)
    @q3.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Right X", correct: true },
      { body: "Right Y", correct: true },
      { body: "Wrong Z", correct: false }
    ])
  end

  test "start_for_quiz! snapshots only active questions in order and generates unique code" do
    game1 = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    game2 = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_not_equal game1.code, game2.code
    assert_equal "lobby", game1.status
    assert_equal [ "Question one", "Question three" ], game1.ordered_questions.map(&:body)
    assert_equal [ "Wrong A", "Right B" ], game1.ordered_questions.first.game_options.map(&:body)
  end

  test "start_for_quiz! raises when quiz has no active questions" do
    empty_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Empty")
    assert_raises(Game::NoActiveQuestionsError) { Game.start_for_quiz!(empty_quiz) }
  end

  test "state machine transitions, answer submission, and no correct-answer leakage while open" do
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    assert game.start!
    assert_not game.start! # idempotent

    assert game.question_open?
    q1 = game.current_question
    assert_equal "Question one", q1.body

    # Security: open payloads must never include :correct or :outcome
    open_public = game.public_player_state
    open_player = game.player_state(alice)
    assert_not open_public.to_json.include?("correct")
    assert_not open_player.to_json.include?("correct")
    assert_not open_player.key?(:outcome)

    wrong_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(body: "Wrong A")
    right_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(body: "Right B")

    # Alice picks wrong then changes to right; last pick counts
    assert_equal wrong_opt.id, game.submit_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_answers_count
    assert_equal right_opt.id, game.submit_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_answers_count

    # Expected question guard prevents closing wrong question
    assert_not game.finish_question!(expected_question_id: q1.id + 999)
    assert game.finish_question!(expected_question_id: q1.id)
    assert_not game.finish_question! # idempotent

    # Cannot submit answers after question is closed
    assert_nil game.submit_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)

    assert_equal "correct", game.player_state(alice)[:outcome]
    assert_equal "no_answer", game.player_state(bob)[:outcome]

    mod_closed = game.moderator_state
    assert_equal false, mod_closed[:question][:is_last]
    opt_counts = mod_closed[:question][:options].index_by { |o| o[:body] }
    assert_equal 0, opt_counts["Wrong A"][:count]
    assert_equal false, opt_counts["Wrong A"][:correct]
    assert_equal 1, opt_counts["Right B"][:count]
    assert_equal true, opt_counts["Right B"][:correct]

    # Cannot end_game before last question
    assert_not game.end_game!

    assert game.next_question!(expected_question_id: q1.id)
    assert_not game.next_question!(expected_question_id: q1.id)
    q3 = game.current_question
    assert_equal "Question three", q3.body
    assert game.last_question?

    assert game.finish_question!(expected_question_id: q3.id)
    assert_not game.next_question!
    assert game.end_game!(expected_question_id: q3.id)
    assert game.finished?
  end

  test "deleting questions or quiz after games exist works cleanly" do
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    @q1.destroy!
    game.reload
    assert_equal 2, game.game_questions.count
    assert_equal "Question one", game.ordered_questions.first.body

    @quiz.destroy!
    assert_equal 0, Game.count
  end
end

class LiveGameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  setup do

    stub_connection(connection_id: "c1", moderator_authenticated: false)

    assert subscription.rejected?

    wrong_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id + 999)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: wrong_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    valid_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: valid_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end

  test "PlayerChannel tracks presence for joined player and ignores anonymous visitor" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    stub_connection(connection_id: "anon-1", moderator_authenticated: false, signed_cookie: nil)
    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
    unsubscribe

    # Joined player increments active players on subscribe and decrements on unsubscribe
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, player.id ])

    stub_connection(connection_id: "alice-1", moderator_authenticated: false, signed_cookie: nil)

    assert_equal 1, @game.active_players_count
    assert_equal "Alice", transmissions.last.dig(:player, :name)

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
  end
end

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      assert_selector "button.play-option[disabled]", count: 3
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) do
      assert_text "Wrong!"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "No answer"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end

    # Moderator advances to Q2 (actually Q3, since Q2 was inactive)
    Capybara.using_session(:moderator) do
      click_button "Next"
      assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      assert_no_text "Inactive hidden question?"
      assert_text "Answers: 0 / 3"
    end

    # All 3 players live-update to Q3 and pick different options (2 correct options!)
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      click_button "HTTP/1.1"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /HTTP\/1\.1.*Your answer/
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      click_button "WebSocket"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /WebSocket.*Your answer/
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) do
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      click_button "UDP"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /UDP.*Your answer/
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 3 / 3"
      click_button "Finish"

      # Last question shows "End quiz" instead of "Next"
      assert_button "End quiz"
      assert_no_button "Next"

      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "HTTP/1.1") do
        assert_text "Correct"
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "WebSocket") do
        assert_text "Correct"
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "UDP") do
        assert_no_text "Correct"
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) { assert_text "Wrong!" }

    # Visitor Dave is sitting on join form before end -> should live-update to "The quiz is over"
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
    end

    # Moderator ends quiz
    Capybara.using_session(:moderator) do
      click_button "End quiz"
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_button "End quiz"
    end

    # Everyone live-updates to "The quiz is over" without page reload
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) do
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_no_button "Join"
    end

    # Brand new visitor opening join link after end sees "The quiz is over" and cannot join
    Capybara.using_session(:eve) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_no_button "Join"
    end
  end

  test "playing same quiz twice creates isolated games and supports URL-embedded basic auth and Wi-Fi recovery" do
    single_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Rehearsal vs Talk")
    q = single_quiz.questions.build(body: "Is Rails awesome?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Yes", correct: true },
      { body: "Totally", correct: true }
    ])

    game1_url = nil
    game2_url = nil

    # Moderator uses URL-embedded Basic Auth (like QA tests sometimes do!)
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_url_auth) do
      server = Capybara.current_session.server
      user = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]
      pass = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]
      visit "http://#{user}:#{pass}@#{server.host}:#{server.port}#{moderate_quiz_path(single_quiz)}"

      click_button "Start a game"
      assert_text "Rehearsal vs Talk"
      game1_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
      assert_not_includes game1_url, pass
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:player_one) do
      visit game1_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"

      # Simulate conference Wi-Fi drop (close WebSocket and go offline via JS / network)
      execute_script("window.Stimulus.controllers.forEach(c => { if (c.consumer) c.consumer.disconnect() })")
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:mod_url_auth) do
      click_button "Start"
      assert_text "Question 1 of 1"
    end

    # Player recovers automatically via online/polling sync without reloading the page!
    Capybara.using_session(:player_one) do
      execute_script("window.dispatchEvent(new Event('online'))")
      assert_text "Is Rails awesome?"
      click_button "Yes"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /Yes.*Your answer/
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:mod_url_auth) do
      assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"
      click_button "Finish"
      # Single-question quiz immediately shows "End quiz"
      assert_button "End quiz"
      assert_no_button "Next"
      click_button "End quiz"
      assert_text "The quiz is over"

      # Start a second game of the same quiz
      click_link "← Back to quiz"
      click_button "Start a game"
      assert_text "Players: 0"
      game2_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
      assert_not_equal game1_url, game2_url
    end

    # Same browser opening Game 2 is asked for name again (fresh player per game),
    # while Game 1 still says "The quiz is over"
    Capybara.using_session(:player_one) do
      visit game2_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"

      visit game1_url
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
    end
  end
end

**A Quick Fix and a Full Test Run**

Alright, that's a classic! I see a simple little stubbing error in `test/channels/live_game_channels_test.rb`. The problem is that the stub `stub_connection(signed_cookie: nil)` is defining a method called `signed_cookie` that expects no arguments. However, the `ApplicationCable::Connection#signed_cookie(name)` method actually requires a `name` argument. That's a textbook mismatch.

A quick lambda or a properly defined method on the stub should fix that right up. No big deal. I'm going to take care of that right away.

Once that's done, I'll run *both* `rails test` and `rails test:system`. Gotta make sure everything's still shipshape and Bristol fashion. Can't be too careful, especially with those system tests. Let's get this done.
