cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > test/channels/live_game_channels_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class LiveGameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Test Quiz")
    q = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Capital of France?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Paris", correct: true },
      { body: "Lyon", correct: false }
    ])
    @game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
  end

  test "ModeratorChannel rejects unauthorized subscribers and accepts valid signed token" do
    self.class.tests ModeratorChannel

    stub_connection(connection_id: "c1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    wrong_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id + 999)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: wrong_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    valid_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: valid_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end

  test "PlayerChannel tracks presence for joined player and ignores anonymous visitor" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    # Anonymous visitor does not increment active players
    stub_connection(connection_id: "anon-1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    connection.define_singleton_method(:signed_cookie) { |_name| nil }
    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
    unsubscribe

    # Joined player increments active players on subscribe and decrements on unsubscribe
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, player.id ])

    stub_connection(connection_id: "alice-1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    connection.define_singleton_method(:signed_cookie) { |_name| nil }
    subscribe(code: @game.code, player_token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_equal 1, @game.active_players_count
    assert_equal "Alice", transmissions.last.dig(:player, :name)

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
  end
end
EOF

**Debugging the Importmap - AHA!**

Okay, here we go... *AHA!* I see it! Let's examine this `importmap.json` output. There it is! The `imports` section clearly outlines the expected JavaScript assets. But wait... something's off. I'm not seeing `moderator_game_controller` or `player_game_controller` listed anywhere in here. That's a problem.

Why aren't they showing up? They *should* be there. This is likely due to stale precompiled assets! We probably have an outdated version of `public/assets/.manifest.json` from before the inclusion of those new controllers. That's it, that must be it! Propshaft is picking up the old manifest instead of the dynamic files, leading to this importmap issue.

Okay, time to confirm. Let's do a quick `ls -la public/assets` to check the assets right now, and see what we're actually working with.

**A Moment of Triumph!**

Okay, hold on a second... *whoa*! Stop everything! I need to take a moment to savor this because I can't believe it! The *entire* live system, with all its complexities, worked on the very *first* run! Live presence (watch those player counts jump! `0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1 -> 2`), the live game start, live questions, the live Wi-Fi recovery mechanism, even URL-embedded basic authentication, and *live answer submission* – every single piece of that puzzle fit perfectly the first time around!

Alright, alright, let's keep cool... gotta find the issue from before to see what was failing! Ah, here it is: the only assertion failure was due to a Ruby regex nuance. Specifically, the test was expecting a single line match, but found the text with newlines between its parts, because the `.play-option` element uses `display: flex`. The code was trying to match this text: `"A\n418\nYour answer"`. In Ruby regex, the `.` character doesn't match newlines unless you use the `/m` (multiline) flag. 

So, all that is left to do is add the `/m` flag to the regex in `test/system/live_game_test.rb`. Then, let's run that *entire* multi-browser live system test from beginning to end and make sure this whole thing is locked down!

**Adversarial Testing Deep Dive: System Robustness**

Okay, so we've got a fantastic set of system tests with no failures, but that's just the starting point. Time to put on the adversarial hat and try to break this thing in every way imaginable! Let's think like a quality assurance engineer and see if we can find any subtle flaws!

Firstly, we're going to dive deep into how Playwright interacts with our UI elements. We'll cross-reference everything using its locators, paying close attention to semantics.

We have a quiz page "Start a game" button, we will check if  `getByRole` has exact matches. What if the start button is disabled when active count is zero and enabled when toggled? We will verify that in question_active_controller.js. Also we will check if button_to places it on the <button> not on the <form>.

Next, we'll scrutinize the lobby big screen: the quiz title, the join link, and the QR code. We'll make sure the join link is visible, selectable, and contains the exact host and port, even with IPv6 or custom hostnames. The QR code must render flawlessly, meeting Chromium standards, and be decodable. We'll check the players count, ensuring proper rendering and accessibility.

On the "Question Open Big Screen," we will verify the progress display, question text, options (each in its own `<li>`), and answer counter. We'll check that the "Finish" button aligns with Playwright's expectations. Similarly, the "Question Closed Big Screen" must have accurate progress, question text, option rendering, and button behavior (Next/End Quiz) for both the moderator and player. We will check the "Finished Big Screen," and the Player Join Page.

We'll dissect the "Player Join Page," including the label, input field, and the button and focus on how the server handles spaces, empty submissions, and normalization of player names.

For the "Player Open Question," we'll analyze the question text, option buttons, and how Playwright's `getByRole` interacts with answer selection. We will double check for correct or any hint in the page source to guarantee no leakage of this information. We are going to make a careful note and check subtle details on the player side when two players are in the game and a player reloads or disconnects, even for the moderator side to make sure that the system acts accordingly.

We will carefully trace a subtle race condition on `PlayerChannel#subscribed`, paying attention to the moderator's actions and how player state is handled during reconnects and disconnections, especially with slow or blocked WebSocket connections. We will look at `app/javascript/controllers/player_game_controller.js` and `app/javascript/controllers/moderator_game_controller.js` to see what happens if `/cable` WebSocket fails to connect initially. And we will add a short grace timer so that HTTP fallback polling AUTOMATICALLY kicks in.

We will also check what happens in `PlayerChannel` and `ModeratorChannel` when `ActionCable` reconnects after clean disconnections and page navigations, tracking how the player count updates and how the system responds to offline states (browser closing, tab closing, Airplane mode). The best balance is that `heartbeat = 3000ms`, `ws_stale_seconds = 10.0`, `http_ttl_seconds = 10.0`, `sweep_interval_seconds = 2.0` because this gives an awesome balance between conference Wi-Fi tolerance and prompt offline detection!

**Refining WebSockets and Connection Recovery in Action Cable**

Okay, let's break this down. First, I need to revisit lines 180-194 of `actioncable.esm.js`. The `Connection#reopen()` method is clever; it handles both the active state, closing and reopening after a `reopenDelay`, *and* the closed state by calling `this.open()` directly. And that `ConnectionMonitor` also checks for a `connectionIsStale()` condition, which is triggered after six seconds without a server ping, leading to a `reopen()`. This is key.

Therefore, in my `recoverConnection()` method, I can consolidate the check. Instead of worrying about separate cases, I can simply use `!this.consumer.connection.isOpen() || this.consumer.connection.monitor.connectionIsStale()` to cover *both* closed sockets *and* those problematic "half-open" connections that go silent. This immediately addresses issues when a device reconnects after losing signal or waking from sleep. Brilliant!

Now, the implementation. I'm going to apply two specific refinements.

1.  **GamePresence Configuration:** Update the defaults: `DEFAULT_WS_STALE_SECONDS` to 10.0, `DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL_SECONDS` to 10.0, and `DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` to 2.0.

2.  **Controller Updates:** For both `moderator_game_controller.js` and `player_game_controller.js`, I'll:

    *   Introduce a 2.5-second initial WS connect grace fallback timer, `this.connectGraceTimer`. This gets cleaned up in `connected()` and `disconnect()`. This is important, as it handles strict conference Wi-Fi firewalls that can stall WebSockets. The HTTP fallback polling will kick in automatically after those 2.5 seconds. Smart!
    *   Update the heartbeat interval in `player_game_controller.js` from 4000 to 3000 ms.
    *   Update the crucial `recoverConnection()` method to use that combined check: `!this.consumer.connection.isOpen() || this.consumer.connection.monitor.connectionIsStale()`.

messages.thinking: **Edge Case Testing: A System Test Deep Dive** Okay, let's ramp up the rigor on this system test. I'm thinking we need to seriously bolster our coverage in `test/system/live_game_test.rb`. These edge cases are calling out for specific attention. Firstly, I'm thinking about the user experience when a player reloads mid-question. If they've already made a selection, the browser should remember their previous answer, but they should *still* be able to change it. That's a critical usability factor that needs to be ironclad. Secondly, let's account for the moderator's perspective. What happens when *they* refresh the big screen mid-question, or even after the game has finished? We need to ensure that the state is cleanly preserved and that all the buttons continue to function flawlessly in real time. Next, the multi-tab scenario. A single player should absolutely *not* be counted as multiple players just because they have multiple tabs open. Tapping an option in one tab must live-sync the `"Your answer"` to the other tab immediately, and closing a tab should correctly update the player count. We need to be absolutely certain our live sync is behaving as expected. And let's make sure the quiz setup and game availability live-sync properly. Toggling all questions inactive should disable the `"Start a game"` button, and toggling just one back on should instantly re-enable it. It needs to react immediately to changes in quiz configuration. Finally, we have to ensure any potentially malicious player input is rendered safely. If a player submits an XSS-like name, like `Alice & "Bob"`, it needs to render as literal text, `"Hi, Alice & "Bob"!"`, without allowing any script execution. This is a critical security vulnerability to eliminate. I’m convinced we need a *third* dedicated system test. Let’s create a new test that comprehensively covers all of these edge cases, and then run the *entire* test suite to make sure nothing breaks in the process. It's time to build a robust and resilient system.

**Production Verification Checklist: Go Time!**

Alright, ALL tests are green! Unit, channel, integration... everything. Now, before we call it done, let's nail down these three crucial production verifications. This is where the rubber meets the road.

First, the *big* one: let's put `bin/serve` through its paces in a *true* `RAILS_ENV=production` environment. Remember the setup: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000` (or a test port, like 3123), plus the necessary secret keys and moderator credentials. `bin/serve` is the key. It preps the database, compiles assets, and fires up the app in production mode, listening on all interfaces via plain HTTP. No SSL, no fancy redirects, just a solid server. It's expecting `/up` to return a `200` when it's ready.

So, the plan:

1.  Run `bin/serve` on a test port.
2.  Wait for that `/up` 200.
3.  Then, get two headless Chromium browsers going (using Ferrum/Cuprite), simulating a live, real game with a Moderator and Player.
4.  Point them at `http://localhost:3123` with a custom Host header for good measure.
5.  **Critical checks during the live game:**
    *   Zero JavaScript console errors in production! This is key.
    *   Confirm ALL the precompiled assets are loading correctly with a 200 OK. Think `actioncable.esm.js`, the game controllers, and the CSS/font files.
    *   Action Cable WebSocket connection `/cable` should establish a `101 Switching Protocols` handshake, even over plain HTTP in production mode.
    *   Verify the *entire* live game flow works flawlessly – no page reloads, a smooth experience.

6.  And then, a clean up of the test production SQLite DB (`storage/production.sqlite3*`), but we need to consider the `public/assets` directory. We should check whether `bin/serve` runs `assets:precompile`. Is `public/assets` clean or up-to-date after running? Remember `test` mode sometimes uses `public/assets/.manifest.json`! We need to check what `bin/serve` does at startup to verify all assets are fresh at startup.

    WAIT!  We saw `public/assets` was precompiled from the last step in the repo!  Running `assets:precompile` *after* all edits guarantees the `.manifest.json` matches the latest code, and `bin/serve` also runs `assets:precompile` (which is fast when up-to-date). It's even better to check if `bin/serve` also runs `assets:clobber`. `assets:precompile` in Propshaft automatically updates that manifest. Still, we should confirm `public/assets/.manifest.json` looks correct after we start `bin/serve`.

Second, let's run `bin/rubocop` and `bin/brakeman`. Gotta catch those linting and security issues before they sneak into production.

Finally, we absolutely *must* update `docs/architecture.md`. It needs clean, focused notes about the live game's architecture: `Game`, `GamePresence`, the Action Cable channels, Wi-Fi resilience considerations, QR generation details – everything that'll make future development smoother.

  player_ctx = browser.contexts.create
  mod_page = mod_ctx.create_page
  player_page = player_ctx.create_page

  js_errors = []
  [mod_page, player_page].each do |p|

  mod_page.network.wait_for_idle

  mod_page.at_xpath("//a[contains(., \"Add question\")]").click
  mod_page.network.wait_for_idle
  mod_page.at_css("#question_body").focus.type("Best language?")
  mod_page.at_css("#question_option_1_body").focus.type("Ruby")
  mod_page.at_css("#question_option_1_correct").click
  mod_page.at_css("#question_option_2_body").focus.type("COBOL")

  player_page.at_css("#player_name").focus.type("Alice")
  player_page.at_xpath("//button[contains(., \"Join\")]").click
  sleep 0.8

  raise "Expected Hi, Alice! on player" unless player_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("Hi, Alice!")

  raise "Expected live Players: 1 on moderator, got: #{mod_text}" unless mod_text.include?("Players: 1")
  puts "Live lobby counter updated: Players: 1!"

  player_text = player_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")

  raise "Expected live question on player" unless player_text.include?("Best language?")
  raise "LEAKED correct in player HTML!" if player_page.body.downcase.include?("correct")
  puts "Live Start worked with zero answer leakage!"

  # 5. Player taps Ruby
  player_page.at_xpath("//button[contains(., \"Ruby\")]").click
  sleep 0.8

  player_text = player_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  mod_text = mod_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  raise "Expected Your answer on player" unless player_text.include?("Your answer")
  raise "Expected Answers: 1 / 1 on moderator, got: #{mod_text}" unless mod_text.include?("Answers: 1 / 1")
  puts "Live answer counter updated: Answers: 1 / 1!"

  # 6. Moderator clicks Finish
  mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space(.)=\"Finish\"]").click
  sleep 0.8

  mod_text = mod_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  player_text = player_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  raise "Expected Correct & End quiz on moderator" unless mod_text.include?("Correct") && mod_text.include?("End quiz")
  raise "Expected Correct! on player, got: #{player_text}" unless player_text.include?("Correct!")
  puts "Live Finish worked: Correct! on player & Correct + End quiz on moderator!"

  mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space(.)=\"End quiz\"]").click
  sleep 0.8

  mod_text = mod_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  player_text = player_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
  raise "Expected The quiz is over on moderator" unless mod_text.include?("The quiz is over")
  raise "Expected The quiz is over on player" unless player_text.include?("The quiz is over")
  puts "Live End quiz worked: The quiz is over on both!"

  browser.quit

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Stimulus, and Action Cable (`async` adapter in single-process Puma). All CSS, JS, QR SVGs (`rqrcode`), and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required). `has_many :game_options, dependent: :nullify`.

### Live Game Tables

- `games`: `quiz_id` (FK), `code` (unique 5-char uppercase code excluding ambiguous glyphs, e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby`, `question_open`, `question_closed`, `finished`), `current_question_index` (0-based), `started_at`, `finished_at`.
- `game_questions`: immutable snapshot of active questions taken when a game is created (`game_id`, nullable `question_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`).
- `game_options`: immutable snapshot of options (`game_question_id`, nullable `option_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`, `correct`).
- `players`: `game_id` (FK), `name` (trimmed, 1..80 chars), `token` (unique random secret stored in a signed per-game cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>`).
- `answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, with a unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]` so answer updates are atomic SQLite upserts and the last pick wins.

Snapshotting `game_questions` and `game_options` preserves historical/in-progress games even if a quiz is edited or questions are deleted later, while retaining `question_id` and `option_id` links for future analytics, leaderboards, and response views.

## Quiz Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with strictly the content keys: `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`), always writing both `active` and `correct` and preserving `position` order. Live game tables (`games`, `players`, `answers`) are never included in export JSON.
- `Moderate::ExportsController#show` (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export`) renders the exported JSON inside the page's sole `<pre>` element (`code-block`), with a Stimulus `copy_code_controller.js` button that works over both HTTPS and plain HTTP.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, structure, types, and all quiz/question rules before creating a new `Quiz` inside a single transaction.
- `Moderate::ImportsController` (`GET /moderate/import`, `POST /moderate/import`) renders the `"Quiz JSON"` form and redirects to the newly created quiz page on success, or re-renders with `422 Unprocessable Entity` on error.

## Live Game Real-Time Architecture & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Moderator area (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games`, `/moderate/games/:id`)**: protected by HTTP Basic Auth (`Moderate::BaseController`). Big screen renders server-side HTML (including an inline crisp-edge SVG QR code from `rqrcode` with 4-module quiet zone) and connects via `moderator_game_controller.js` to `ModeratorChannel` (`game:<id>:moderator`), authorized via HTTP Basic Auth or a cryptographically signed per-game token (`MessageVerifier(:moderator_stream)`).
- **Player area (`/play/:code`)**: public, no auth required. Players join with a name and are remembered per game via a signed `httponly` cookie (`quizzy_player_<CODE>`). `player_game_controller.js` connects to `PlayerChannel` (`game:<id>:players` + `game:<id>:player:<player_id>`).
- **Zero correct-answer leakage**: `Game#public_player_state`, `Game#player_state`, `/play/:code` HTML, `/play/:code/state`, and `/play/:code/answer` omit `correct` and `outcome` until `status == "question_closed"`.
- **Real-time active player presence (`GamePresence`)**: thread-safe in-memory tracker deduplicating multiple tabs per player, combining immediate WebSocket connect/disconnect tracking with a short HTTP grace window (eliminating join/reload races) and a 3s client heartbeat + 10s stale-connection sweeper for silent Wi-Fi drops.
- **Conference Wi-Fi resilience**:
  - Action Cable WebSocket connections immediately transmit full state snapshots on every connect and reconnect.
  - Monotonic state-rank guards prevent out-of-order broadcasts or delayed polls from reverting UI state.
  - Automatic HTTP polling fallback activates if WebSocket disconnects or takes >2.5s to connect; `online`, `visibilitychange`, and `pageshow` trigger immediate reconnect + state resync.
  - Answer taps use a serialized latest-wins queue with automatic retry on transient network failures; `"Your answer"` is confirmed once persisted in SQLite, and in-place DOM updates prevent detaching buttons mid-click.
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` prevents stale proxy/browser caching.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, enforcing HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- `GET /up`, `GET /`, and `/play/:code*` do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- All `fetch()` and WebSocket URLs resolve against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so URL-embedded Basic Auth works reliably across HTTP and WebSockets.
- `question_active_controller.js` updates question numbering, active summary, and the `"Start a game"` button disabled state live as checkboxes are toggled.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`). `config/database.yml` allocates `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` SQLite connections to serve Puma threads and Action Cable workers cleanly without contention.
EOF
